newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: CVG says Placer's Las Cristinas project secure.
newsitem.headline: CVG says Placer's Las Cristinas project secure.

text.p: Venezuelan state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG) said Monday its joint venture with Canadian mining company Placer Dome Inc would not be affected by a property claim on the Las Cristinas concession.
The claim, by mining rival Crystallex International Corp, "will not affect the development of the project," CVG spokesman Adrian Vasquez told Reuters.
"Legally, Crystallex doesn't have a right to the concessions," added Vasquez. The CVG holds a 30 percent stake in the $576 million project.

Early Monday, Crystallex said it had acquired a Venezuelan company with long-held rights to the disputed Las Cristinas blocks. Those rights were recently upheld by a Surpreme Count ruling, the company said.
Crystallex and Placer Dome officials in Caracas declined to comment. Industry sources said, however, it was unlikely Placer would lose the concession -- despite the Supreme Court ruling.
"It's confusing, but the outcome will most likely be: Placer will keep the concession," said the source, who asked not to be identified.
"Meanwhile Crystallex's claim could be expropriated and the company subsequently indemnified."
The confusion highlights the renowned inefficiency of Venezuela's creaking legal system, added the source.
